notes.text: The mountains — Of Judea, to which these glad tidings were brought, and from which they were spread abroad into other countries. Of him - Or, of them; the singular number being put for the plural. Returneth - In the days of the Messiah, God did discover and exercise his dominion over the world far more eminently than ever he had done from the beginning of the world until that time.

Thy watchmen — Thy ministers, who descry the approach of this heavenly king. Lift up thy voice - To give notice to all people of these glad tidings; and by way of exultation, to sing forth the praises of God for this glorious day. Eye - Distinctly and familiarly, their eyes beholding the eyes of this king of glory. They shall be eye and ear-witnesses of the words and works of Christ, and therefore their testimony shall be more certain and valuable. Bring again - When God shall complete the work of bringing his church out of captivity.

glossa.text:
*How beautiful.* ((ID.)) Of him who had said above: *I myself who spoke, behold I am here,* the prophet testifies that he himself preached the Gospel upon the mountains.

*Of him that announceth,* Christ, by himself, by the apostles, to whom he says: *Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you ((Joan. XIV))*. Sitting upon whom the Lord preached: they are also the feet of Christ, by carrying his preaching.
*The voice of the watchmen:* ((ID.)) of the apostles and of the others who are always in the watchtower, that they may foresee all things and advance those subject to them.
*Rejoice.* He consoles the primitive Church, etc., *as far as* by the multitude of the Gentiles it has been both repaired and multiplied.
*The arm. In my arm shall the Gentiles hope ((Psal. XCVII))*. And elsewhere: *Thy arm with power ((Psal. LXXXVIII))*.

notes.text: Salvation — The redemption of the world by the Messiah: which was hitherto reserved was a secret among the Jews, yea was not throughly known by the most of the Jews themselves. Righteousness - His faithfulness in accomplishing this great promise. Israel is required to praise God, for their hasty constitution both in church and state, ver. 1-5. Some instances of the happy administration of it, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text:
*Sing ye to the Lord.* ((CASS.)) First he speaks of the showing forth of the saving right hand.

*He hath saved.* ((AUG.)) It is a greater thing that he raised up the whole world from eternal death, than that he raised the dead. *To himself.* Many are saved bodily, but to themselves, not to him: they who, having received bodily health, grow wanton, but they who by faith are healed within, are healed to him, or save themselves.

*Salvation . . . justice.* ((AUG.)) He who saves and justifies. *He hath revealed.* Things to come were foretold under a veil by the prophets: but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth.*

*Of mercy and of truth.* ((AUG.)) *Mercy* is that whereby he promised, *truth* follows upon this, because he rendered it. But to whom? *To Israel,* that is, to him who now by faith sees the truth, afterwards by sight.
*All.* ((ID.)) Because Christ was not given to certain men only.
*Rejoice ye.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he says that in all ways he is to be praised and declared, because the judge is come.

*With ductile trumpets and with the voice of a trumpet of horn.* ((AUG.)) Of brass, which are drawn out by beating, etc., *as far as* as the horn cleaves to the flesh, and surpasses it. ((HIERON.)) With ductile trumpets, of silver, after the manner of the Jews. Mystically, drawn out under the hammer of the whole earth, that is, the devil. ((AUG.)) Tribulation is the beating; advancement, the drawing out: such a trumpet was Job, whence he sounded as a trumpet, saying: *The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away.*

*Let it be moved.* ((ID.)) That is, let the sea of the law be made sweet, the wood of the cross being set therein. *And the fulness thereof.* All the sacraments of the law, etc., *as far as* but *the rivers,* etc. *The earth.* ((CASS.)) That is, every sinner.

*The world of the earth.* All earthly men. *In justice.* ((AUG.)) Because they did not merit mercy. *The peoples.* ((CASS.)) The faithful out of the Jews and the Gentiles, who shall receive things equal to their merits.

notes.text: The proposition and sum, 5-9

The treatise itself. We have a perfect author of salvation, who suffered for our sake, that he might be, (1.) a merciful, and (2.) a faithful, (3.) high priest,. 10-13 These three are particularly explained, his passion and consummation being continually interwoven

1. He has the virtues of an high priest a. He is faithful, iii.1 Therefore be ye not unfaithful iv.13 b. He is merciful, 15 Therefore come to him with confidence v.3

2. He is called of God an high priest. Here, a. The sum is proposed, 4-10 With a summary exhortation 11- vi. 20 b. The point is copiously,

1. Explained. We have a great high priest,

1. Such as is described in the hundred and tenth Psalm After the order of Melchisedec, vii. 1-19 Established by an oath, 20-22 For ever, 23-28

2. Therefore peculiarly excellent-Heavenly, viii. 1-6 Of the new covenant, 7-13 By whom we have an entrance into the sanctuary ix. 1 x. 18

2. Applied. Therefore,

1. Believe, hope, love 19-25 These three are farther inculcated, a. Faith, with patience, 26-39 Which, after the example of the ancients,. xi.1 xii.1 And of Christ himself, 2, 3 Is to be exercised, 4-11 Cheerfully, peaceably, holily, 12-17 b. Hope, 18-20 c. Love, C.xiii. 1-6

2. In order to grow in these graces, make use of The remembrance of your former, 7-16 The vigilance of your present, pastors, 17-19 To this period, and to the whole epistle, answers The prayer, the doxology, and the mild conclusion, 20-25 There are many comparisons in this epistle, which may be nearly reduced to two heads:

1. The prophets, the angels, Moses, Joshua, Aaron, are great; but Jesus Christ is infinitely greater

2. The ancient believers enjoyed high privileges; but Christian believers enjoy far higher. To illustrate this, examples both of happiness and misery are everywhere interspersed: so that in this epistle there is a kind of recapitulation of the whole Old Testament. In this also Judaism is abrogated, and Christianity carried to its height. HEBREWS

Who sat down — The third of these glorious predicates, with which three other particulars are interwoven, which are mentioned likewise, and in the same order, Colossians i, 15, 17, 20. Who, being - The glory which he received in his exaltation at the right hand of the Father no angel was capable of; but the Son alone, who likewise enjoyed it long before. The brightness of his glory - Glory is the nature of God revealed in its brightness. The express image - Or stamp. Whatever the Father is, is exhibited in the Son, as a seal in the stamp on wax. Of his person - Or substance. The word denotes the unchangeable perpetuity of divine life and power. And sustaining all things - Visible and invisible, in being. By the word of his power - That is, by his powerful word. When he had by himself - Without any Mosaic rites or ceremonies. Purged our sins - In order to which it was necessary he should for a time divest himself of his glory. In this chapter St. Paul describes his glory chiefly as he is the Son of God; afterwards, ver. 6, &c., the glory of the man Christ Jesus. He speaks, indeed, briefly of the former before his humiliation, but copiously after his exaltation; as from hence the glory he had from eternity began to be evidently seen. Both his purging our sins, and sitting on the right hand of God, are largely treated of in the seven following chapters. Sat down - The priests stood while they ministered: sitting, therefore, denotes the consummation of his sacrifice. This word, sat down, contains the scope, the theme, and the sum, of the epistle.

This verse has two clauses, the latter of which is treated of, ver. 5; the former, ver. 13. Such transpositions are also found in the other epistles of St. Paul, but in none so frequently as in this. The Jewish doctors were peculiarly fond of this figure, and used it much in all their writings. The apostle therefore, becoming all things to all men, here follows the same method. All the inspired writers were readier in all the figures of speech than the most experienced orators. Being — By his exaltation, after he had been lower than them, chap. ii, 9. So much higher than the angels - It was extremely proper to observe this, because the Jews gloried in their law, as it was delivered by the ministration of angels. How much more may we glory in the gospel, which was given, not by the ministry of angels, but of the very Son of God! As he hath by inheritance a more excellent name - Because he is the Son of God, he inherits that name, in right whereof he inherits all things His inheriting that name is more ancient than all worlds; his inheriting all things, as ancient as all things. Than they - This denotes an immense preeminence. The angels do not inherit all things, but are themselves a portion of the Son's inheritance, whom they worship as their Lord.

glossa.text: *Of old.* It is not new. *God,* who is unchangeable then and now. *Speaking.* He says: *speaking,* in the present, because what was then is even now. *To the fathers.* That is, to those who are fathers to us in flesh and in the worship of God. *In the prophets.* For not they themselves, but God in them. *In divers manners.* That is, many times to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the rest, and often to the same men. *And in many ways.* Because now by dreams, as to Daniel: now by an open voice, as to Moses: now by inward inspiration, as to David.

*In the Son,* who is greater than the prophets. For he is the fulfiller and sanctifier of the prophets. Thus then he is a prophet, in that he is also the Lord of the prophets. So too Christ is an angel, in that he is also the Lord of the angels. *He appointed* unchangeably. *Heir of all things,* that is, possessor of every creature. For Jacob is no longer the portion of the Lord, and Israel his part: but absolutely all the nations of the world.

*Who being the brightness of his glory,* etc. Here he commends Christ according to his divine nature, showing him coeternal and coequal with the Father, and of the same substance with him, but other in person.

*The figure of his substance.* Behold, otherwise, personally, as a figure from him whose figure it is. But equal, because not unlike, as he himself says: *The Father is in me;* and: *He that seeth me, seeth my Father also ((Joan. XIV))*. Note that these names, namely light, glory, are sometimes referred to the divine nature, sometimes to the person. And when they are referred to the person; they are referred now to the Father, now to the Son. For we say: The Father is light, and the Son is light. Likewise the Father is glory, the Son glory, and these two are one glory and one light, not two. And the Son is called glory of glory, as light of light, and beginning of beginning, and God of God, yet not two gods, but one, not two beginnings, but one. But brightness and figure, as image also, are properly referred to the person of the Son and are said relatively.

 *And upholding all things,* etc. It was said above that through him he made all things. Here he now attributes to him the sum of authority, from this, that with authority he governs and holds together all things. For as all things were created by him, so through him, who is unchangeable, they are preserved. For the omnipotence of the Creator is the cause of subsisting to every creature, and if that power should at any time cease from ruling the things it founded, at once the form and nature of all things would fall together.

*Purgation.* After he has shown the excellence of him by whom he created and governs all things, here he commends the kindness of his humility. For he puts us in mind of the cross and the resurrection and the ascension, where he says: *He sitteth,* etc. *On high.* In saying this, he does not shut God up in a place: but shows the man Christ loftier than all and more eminent than all. So also by the right hand he did not give God a shape, but showed the likeness of honour. For he that hath confessed *Confessus*; read *consessus*, "the sitting together" shows nothing else but equality of honour.

*So much better.* Yet in the psalm he says: *He was made a little less than the angels ((Psal. VIII))*. Here he is said to be better than the same. And as that was said according to his human nature, so this too could be understood to have been said according to the divine, were it not that *made* is added, by which it is opened that here he speaks of him according to the flesh. For according to that whereby he is acknowledged consubstantial with the substance of the Father, he was not made, but born: the discourse therefore is of him according to his human nature, according to which he was both less than the angels in his passion, and greater and better also in the fulness of grace, of which the angels themselves also receive by measure.

*A more differing name.* While he was mortal, he had a differing name, because the angels ministered to him. After he was immortal, more differing still. And because he could have this, and not for them, he adds *than they,* that is, greatly differing from the name of the angels, this is the name which is above every name, namely God, or Son, which is truly worthier than that by which they are called angels, that is, messengers. For the name of Son shows what is proper, not adoption, because unless he were the proper Son, the Apostle could not from this assert the greatness of his honour. But the proper Son is begotten of the Father himself. But if he were Son by the grace of adoption, he would be less not only than the Father, but even than the angels.

4. The conclusion 24, 25 THE GOSPEL OF JOHN

In him was life — He was the foundation of life to every living thing, as well as of being to all that is. And the life was the light of men - He who is essential life, and the giver of life to all that liveth, was also the light of men; the fountain of wisdom, holiness, and happiness, to man in his original state.
And the light shineth in darkness — Shines even on fallen man; but the darkness - Dark, sinful man, perceiveth it not.
There was a man — The evangelist now proceeds to him who testified of the light, which he had spoken of in the five preceding verses.

The same came for (that is, in order to give) a testimony — The evangelist, with the most strong and tender affection, interweaves his own testimony with that of John, by noble digressions, wherein he explains the office of the Baptist; partly premises and partly subjoins a further explication to his short sentences. What St. Matthew, Mark, and Luke term the Gospel, in respect of the promise going before, St. John usually terms the testimony, intimating the certain knowledge of the relator; to testify of the light - Of Christ.

Who lighteth every man — By what is vulgarly termed natural conscience, pointing out at least the general lines of good and evil. And this light, if man did not hinder, would shine more and more to the perfect day.
He was in the world — Even from the creation.
He came — In the fulness of time, to his own - Country, city, temple: And his own - People, received him not.

But as many as received him — Jews or Gentiles; that believe on his name - That is, on him. The moment they believe, they are sons; and because they are sons, God sendeth forth the Spirit of his Son into their hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

Who were born — Who became the sons of God, not of blood - Not by descent from Abraham, nor by the will of the flesh - By natural generation, nor by the will of man - Adopting them, but of God - By his Spirit.

Flesh sometimes signifies corrupt nature; sometimes the body; sometimes, as here, the whole man. We beheld his glory — We his apostles, particularly Peter, James, and John, Luke ix, 32. Grace and truth - We are all by nature liars and children of wrath, to whom both grace and truth are unknown. But we are made partakers of them, when we are accepted through the Beloved. The whole verse might be paraphrased thus: And in order to raise us to this dignity and happiness, the eternal Word, by a most amazing condescension, was made flesh, united himself to our miserable nature, with all its innocent infirmities. And he did not make us a transient visit, but tabernacled among us on earth, displaying his glory in a more eminent manner, than even of old in the tabernacle of Moses. And we who are now recording these things beheld his glory with so strict an attention, that we can testify, it was in every respect such a glory as became the only begotten of the Father. For it shone forth not only in his transfiguration, and in his continual miracles, but in all his tempers, ministrations, and conduct through the whole series of his life. In all he appeared full of grace and truth: he was himself most benevolent and upright; made those ample discoveries of pardon to sinners, which the Mosaic dispensation could not do: and really exhibited the most substantial blessings, whereas that was but a shadow of good things to come.

glossa.text: *In the beginning was the Word.* Against those who, on account of Christ's temporal nativity, said that Christ had not always been, he begins with the eternity of the Word, saying: *In the beginning was the Word.*

*All things were made by him. ((AUG.))* He is not a creature, through whom every creature was made, etc., *as far as* which all agree unto the power of the Divinity.

*And without him was made nothing. ((ORIG.))* Thus he divides it: *And without him was made nothing.* The order is: *There is nothing which was made without him.*
*What was made, was life in him. ((AUG.))* John Chrysostom: *And without him was made nothing. What was made.* Hilary: *Without him was made nothing, which was made in him.*

*There was a man sent.* After he had ascended by a lofty flight beyond every nature into the height of theology, because he had contemplated that the Word had always been with the Father, he presently descends to the lowliness of human nature, and particularly of the Word's forerunner, against those who said that human nature had been in the first parent wholly lost and brought to nothing. *A man sent.* A man, not an angel, as the heretics will have it, sent from God. Therefore he was able to speak of God.

*He was the true light.* Every man is said to be that nature in man which was made to the image and to the likeness of God. All the other things which are in man are the lower parts of man, and are in a manner outside the man. In that, namely, the soul, as in a certain higher world, the true light shines, and it enlightens those coming into that world and being born again through grace, because they whose life and conversation is in the heavens are as it were in another world.
*And his own received him not.* From the beginning of the world there was no time in which there were not receivers of the divine word; whence he adds: *But as many as received him.*

*To be made the sons of God.* A wondrous power, that they who were sons of the devil should, set free through him, be called both sons of God and brethren of Christ. But by what order they are made sons of God, and how this generation differs from the carnal, is subjoined: *Who not of bloods.*

*And the Word was made flesh.* But that we may securely believe that men are born of God, he subjoins that God is born of man: by this taking on of infirmity our infirmity is healed, that we may be able to be made sons of God. And this is it: *And the Word was made flesh.* That which was above descended below. What wonder: if that which was below ascended into that which is above? Nor is it a wonder if men are born of God, since God was born of man. *Full of grace and truth.* The man Christ was full of grace, because, with no merits going before, from the time he was conceived the Godhead was in him, filling that man with all fullness, redounding into all the saints; whence his mother also is called not only the mother of a man, but also the mother of God. Nor is it a wonder if a man is also called God, since God is also called man. And this is called grace and truth, because it was so promised of old and now exhibited: namely, that God should be in the man, filling him with every good, and through him his own.

echoes.text: For she is a breath of the power of God, and a clear effluence of the glory of the Almighty; therefore can nothing defiled find entrance into her. For she is an effulgence from everlasting light, and an unspotted mirror of the working of God, and an image of his goodness. (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25–26)
echoes.note: The marquee echo of the chapter. ‘Radiance of his glory… the very image of his substance’ (v. 3) reproduces the rare term apaugasma and the eikōn/glory pairing of Wis 7:25–26 — high verbal volume against a Second Temple text most scholars (Hays, Attridge, Beale & Carson) name as the direct source. Hebrews transfers what Wisdom says of personified Sophia to the Son. Confidence kept high despite low text-field availability, since bible-api serves only the Protestant canon.

echoes.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.’
echoes.note: ‘Sat down on the right hand of the Majesty’ (v. 3) is a low-volume echo of Ps 110:1, planted before the catena begins and paid off as its explicit climax at 1:13. Hays' recurrence test: the same source surfaces twice, so even the faint first instance earns credence.

echoes.text: For on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins you shall be clean before Yahweh. (Leviticus 16:30)
echoes.note: ‘When he had by himself purified us of our sins’ (v. 3) quotes nothing, yet figurally invokes the Day of Atonement cult that chapters 9–10 will expound — the book's central typology. No verbal volume; high figural coherence (Hays, Reading Backwards).

echoes.text: Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed. When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born; while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world. When he established the heavens, I was there; when he set a circle on the surface of the deep, when he established the clouds above, when the springs of the deep became strong, when he gave to the sea its boundary, that the waters should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the earth; then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him, rejoicing in his whole world. My delight was with the sons of men.
echoes.note: ‘Through whom also he made the worlds’ (v. 2) draws on the Wisdom-as-agent-of-creation tradition that runs from Prov 8:22–31 into Wisdom and Sirach. Thematic coherence (Wisdom christology) more than verbal volume; the LXX of Prov 8:22 (‘the Lord created me’) fed the patristic debates this verse anticipates.

echoes.text: Ask of me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession.
echoes.note: ‘Whom he appointed heir of all things’ (v. 2) sounds the inheritance grant of Ps 2:8 — the same psalm quoted outright at 1:5. Recurrence (Hays): Ps 2 is demonstrably available and re-used, so the inheritance language is heard as its anticipatory echo.

echoes.text: Dominion was given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom that which will not be destroyed.
echoes.note: ‘Heir of all things’ and the universal, unending dominion granted the one ‘like a son of man’ (Dan 7:14) share thematic coherence with the Son's inheritance and session. Faint, contested — no verbal volume — but a stock messianic substrate scholars note behind the exaltation language.

echoes.text: Yahweh, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: ‘I am Yahweh, who makes all things; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself;’
echoes.note: ‘Upholding all things by the word of his power’ (v. 3) ascribes to the Son the sole-creator role Isa 44:24 reserves to YHWH — a faint conceptual echo that prepares the bolder Ps 102 transfer at 1:10–12. Low volume; coherence with the creation theme of the prologue.

echoes.text: For who in the skies can be compared to Yahweh? Who among the sons of the heavenly beings is like Yahweh,
echoes.note: ‘Having become so much better than the angels’ (v. 4) faintly recalls the incomparability formula of Ps 89:6, which sets YHWH above the ‘sons of the heavenly beings.’ A dashed echo seeding the angel-comparison the catena exists to make; Ps 89 recurs at 1:6 (‘firstborn’).

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: John opens with the exact phrase 'In the beginning' (en archē), the LXX incipit of Genesis 1:1, signaling a deliberate re-narration of creation. Volume is maximal (verbatim phrase in the most marked position of the Gospel) and recurrence strong (creation language saturates vv.1-5). Thematic coherence is total: John reads the Genesis creation through the lens of the Word as agent.

echoes.text: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
echoes.note: Creation 'by the word' ('Let there be light') is recast as creation 'through him,' the Logos (v.3). The Genesis pattern of God speaking the world into being is the conceptual substrate for 'all things were made through him.' High thematic coherence between divine speech-act and the personified Word.

echoes.text: By Yahweh’s word, the heavens were made; all their army by the breath of his mouth.
echoes.note: 'By the word of the LORD the heavens were made' is the clearest OT text crediting creation to God's spoken word, the Jewish exegetical bridge from Genesis to a creative Logos. Strong thematic coherence with v.3 ('all things were made through him') and availability secure in Second-Temple liturgy.

echoes.text: “Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed. When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born; while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world. When he established the heavens, I was […]
echoes.note: Personified Wisdom, 'with' God 'in the beginning' as the agent/craftsman of creation, is the primary background for the Word who 'was with God' and through whom all things were made. Recurrence of the with-God-at-creation motif and high thematic coherence; widely recognized as John's Wisdom-Christology source.

echoes.text: For she that is the architect of all things taught me, even wisdom. For there is in her a spirit quick of understanding, holy, Alone in kind, manifold, Subtil, freely moving, Clear in utterance, unpolluted, Distinct, unharmed, Loving what is good, keen, unhindered, Beneficent, loving toward man, Stedfast, sure, free from care, All-powerful, all-surveying, And penetrating through all spirits That are quick of understanding, pure, most subtle: For wisdom is […]
echoes.note: Wisdom as the 'breath of the power of God,' a pure effulgence of glory, an unspotted mirror, and the light surpassing all light underwrites John's identification of the Word with life and light (vv.4-5). Availability secure (deuterocanonical, first century) and strong thematic coherence with the light/glory motifs of the Prologue.

echoes.text: Wisdom will praise herself, And will glory in the midst of her people. In the congregation of the Most High will she open her mouth, And glory in the presence of his power. I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, And covered the earth as a mist. I lived in high places, And my throne is in the pillar of the cloud. Alone I compassed the circuit of heaven, And walked in the depth of the abyss. In the waves of the sea, and in all the earth, And in every […]
echoes.note: Wisdom's self-praise, coming forth from the mouth of the Most High and present from the beginning, is a key model for the pre-existent Word. Sirach 24 is the most sustained Wisdom-tabernacle hymn and is recurrent across the Prologue (see also v.14). High thematic coherence.

echoes.text: O God of the fathers, and Lord who keep your mercy, Who made all things by your word; And by your wisdom you formedst man, That he should have dominion over the creatures that were made by you,
echoes.note: 'O God... who made all things by your word, and by your wisdom formed man' explicitly pairs word and wisdom as co-agents of creation, the exact fusion John performs on the Logos. Medium confidence because it is conceptual parallel rather than verbal, but thematic coherence with v.3 is high.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: The darkness over the deep before the first light is evoked by 'the light shines in the darkness' (v.5). The creation-from-darkness sequence reinforces the Genesis 1 framing; medium confidence as the verbal contact is thematic (light/darkness) rather than lexical.

echoes.text: For with you is the spring of life. In your light shall we see light.
echoes.note: 'For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light' fuses life and light as divine gifts, exactly the pairing of v.4 ('in him was life, and the life was the light of men'). Thematic coherence is high; flagged medium for absence of verbal borrowing.

echoes.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
echoes.note: 'The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light' offers the light-shining-in-darkness topos. Low confidence and somewhat contested: the motif is broad and could derive from several light texts, but it coheres with the Prologue's darkness-versus-light contest.

echoes.text: For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Whoever finds me finds life' links personified Wisdom directly to life, supporting the life-in-the-Word claim of v.4. Faint and contested, but coherent with the broader Wisdom substrate already established.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: 'Behold, I send my messenger' frames John as the divinely sent forerunner ('there came a man, sent from God'). The sending-of-the-messenger motif is the standard prophetic preparation pattern and coheres with John's witness role; medium because the verbal link is conceptual.

echoes.text: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
echoes.note: 'A light to the nations' resonates with 'the true light that enlightens everyone' (v.9), the universal scope of illumination. Low confidence: the universalizing of light is a shared Isaianic theme rather than a direct quotation.

echoes.text: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
echoes.note: 'The LORD is my light and my salvation' supplies the divine-light identification that the Prologue transfers to the Logos. Faint and contested; included for recurrence of the light-as-God motif.

echoes.text: With all these I sought rest; And in whose inheritance shall I lodge? Then the Creator of all things gave me a commandment; And he that created me made my tabernacle to rest, And said, Let your tabernacle be in Jacob, And your inheritance in Israel. He created me from the beginning before the world; And to the end I will not fail. In the holy tabernacle I ministered before him; And so was I established in Sion. In the beloved city likewise he gave me […]
echoes.note: Wisdom seeks a resting place among the nations and is given Israel as her inheritance; the motif of the agent of creation coming to her own people who variously receive or reject her underlies vv.10-11. Thematic coherence with the Wisdom-rejection pattern is strong; medium for lack of verbal contact.

echoes.text: Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention; but you have ignored all my counsel, and wanted none of my reproof; I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you; when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when your disaster comes on like a whirlwind; when distress and anguish come on you. Then will they call on me, but I will not answer. They will seek me diligently, […]
echoes.note: Wisdom calls but is not received ('I called and you refused'), the rejection-of-Wisdom topos behind 'his own didn't receive him' (v.11). The motif of the personified divine agent spurned by her people coheres tightly with John's tragic note.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: Wisdom finds no dwelling place among humans and returns to heaven, the most pointed Second-Temple parallel to the Word coming to his own and being rejected (vv.10-11). Pseudepigraphal but genuinely warranted here: the Wisdom-withdrawal pattern matches John's reversal closely. Contested as to direct dependence.

echoes.text: You are the children of Yahweh your God. You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.
echoes.note: 'You are the children of the LORD your God' supplies the divine-sonship category recast as the 'right to become God's children' (v.12). Low confidence; the sonship-of-God-people motif is broad across the OT.

echoes.text: Of the Rock who became your father, you are unmindful, and have forgotten God who gave you birth.
echoes.note: 'The God who gave you birth' offers a God-as-begetter image behind 'born... of God' (v.13). Faint and contested, but coheres with the divine-generation language that replaces ordinary descent.

echoes.text: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: 'You are children of the living God,' the promise of new divine sonship to those who were not a people, resonates with becoming God's children by birth from God (vv.12-13). Low confidence; thematic rather than verbal.

echoes.text: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
echoes.note: 'The Word became flesh and lived (eskēnōsen, 'tabernacled') among us' deliberately evokes the sanctuary that God commanded so he might 'dwell among them.' The tabernacle-pitching verb is the load-bearing figural cue: the incarnate Word is the new tent of meeting. High volume and thematic coherence.

echoes.text: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle. Moses wasn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle.
echoes.note: The glory of the LORD filling the tabernacle is the template for 'we saw his glory' (v.14): the indwelling Word manifests the kabod that once filled the tent. The tabernacle-plus-glory pairing makes the figural reading near-certain. High coherence and recurrence with the Sinai cycle.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: 'Full of grace and truth' renders the LXX/Hebrew formula 'abounding in steadfast love (hesed) and faithfulness ('emet)' from God's self-revelation to Moses. This is the densest verbal-conceptual borrowing of the Prologue's climax (vv.14,17). Very high thematic coherence: the glory Israel saw at Sinai is now seen in the Word.

echoes.text: He said, “Please show me your glory.” He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.” He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.” Yahweh also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock. It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of […]
echoes.note: Moses' request to see God's glory, granted only as a passing of God's goodness while his face remains unseen, undergirds both 'we saw his glory' and 'no one has seen God at any time' (vv.14,18). The contrast (Moses denied the face; the Son makes God known) is structured directly on this scene.

echoes.text: He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
echoes.note: 'No one has seen God at any time' (v.18) closely restates 'you cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live.' High volume and a near-citation level of verbal coherence; the Son's making-God-known answers the Sinai limitation.

echoes.text: Then the Creator of all things gave me a commandment; And he that created me made my tabernacle to rest, And said, Let your tabernacle be in Jacob, And your inheritance in Israel.
echoes.note: Wisdom is commanded to 'pitch her tent (kataskēnōson) in Jacob,' the closest Second-Temple antecedent to the Word tabernacling among us (v.14). The tent-pitching verb plus the creation-agent identity makes Sirach 24 a primary source for the whole Prologue. High coherence and recurrence.

echoes.text: He gave to Moses, when he finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets, written with God’s finger.
echoes.note: 'The law was given through Moses' (v.17) refers to the Sinai giving of the tablets 'written with the finger of God.' The Moses-law / Christ-grace antithesis is built on the Sinai law-giving as its foil. Secure availability and strong thematic coherence.

echoes.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him. When Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near him. Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them. […]
echoes.note: Moses' face shining with reflected glory after seeing God contrasts with the Son who is himself the glory and declares the Father (vv.14,18). The Sinai-radiance scene reinforces the Moses-versus-Word comparison; medium for absence of direct verbal borrowing here.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of words, but you saw no form; you only heard a voice.
echoes.note: At Horeb Israel heard a voice but 'saw no form,' the unseen-God theme behind v.18. The motif of God unseen yet now declared by the Son coheres with John's Sinai contrast; medium confidence.

echoes.text: then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,
echoes.note: Wisdom beside God as the delighting child/craftsman supports 'the one and only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father' (v.18), the intimate, eternal closeness of the agent to God. Coheres with the Wisdom substrate established in the opening; medium.

echoes.text: For she is a breath of the power of God, And a clear effluence of the glory of the Almighty; Therefore can nothing defiled find entrance into her. For she is an effulgence from everlasting light, And an unspotted mirror of the working of God, And an image of his goodness.
echoes.note: Wisdom as the radiance of God's glory and image of his goodness underlies 'we saw his glory' and the Son as the one who makes the unseen God known (vv.14,18). Reinforces the glory/visibility theme; medium for conceptual rather than verbal link.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh is slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, forgiving iniquity and disobedience; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation.’
echoes.note: The 'grace and truth' (hesed-we-emet) divine-attribute formula recurs in Moses' intercession, strengthening recurrence of the Exodus 34:6 source behind v.14/17. Listed low because Exodus 34:6 is the primary locus; this is a secondary witness.

echoes.text: Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
echoes.note: 'Steadfast love and faithfulness meet together' pairs hesed and 'emet, the same word-pair behind 'grace and truth.' Faint and contested as a direct source, but evidences the recurrence of the formula in Israel's vocabulary.

harmony.title: The Word made flesh
harmony.note: John alone begins before time itself — "In the beginning was the Word" — where the others begin with a birth or a baptism.

registers.label: Spare
lines: In the beginning was the Word.
And the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The light shines in the darkness.
And the darkness has not overcome it.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
We have seen his glory, full of grace and truth.
Come, let us worship the Word made flesh.
Glory to God in the highest! Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Before the first morning, before the stars were hung, the Word was already there, and the Word was God.
Glory to God in the highest!
Into the deep dark of the world that light came shining, and all the darkness could not put it out.
Glory to God in the highest!
And the Word became flesh — bone of our bone, breath of our breath — and pitched his tent among us.
Glory to God in the highest!
We have seen his glory with our own eyes, full of grace and truth. Come and behold him.
Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth! Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Before all things, the Word was with God.
Glory to God in the highest!
The light shines, and the dark cannot put it out.
Glory to God in the highest!
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
Glory to God in the highest!
Come, let us worship and behold his glory.
Glory to God in the highest! Amen.
